execution_notes: User authorized the October 30 and October 31 first tasks together on October 30. Planned ownership/hours and all later dates remain unchanged; see docs/handoffs/2026-10-30_days-01-02.md for evidence.

days.title: Choose one runnable implementation
days.why: The remote prototype has a UI, while the local branch has reusable modules. Select one integration route before changing either version.
days.need: The two inspected revisions, supplied proposal and current course requirements.
steps: Keep the existing Chroma, MiniLM and Gradio route. Select one Apple 10-K with comparative years; record a minimal scope and launch path.
Define the evidence record and answer status fields. Record which UI functions and local modules will be reused in the integration branch.
Create the acceptance checklist and a shared handoff file. Record the official delivery requirements, model-access assumption and November 17 cutoff.
days.done: One integration checklist, one proposed filing, shared record examples and a fixed delivery checklist are saved.
days.learn: The goal is to repair a small existing prototype and prove its answers, rather than start another implementation.

days.title: Make setup and launch reproducible
days.why: The next owners need a working environment and a single application entry point. Repair setup before spending time on model or retrieval changes.
days.need: The Day 1 integration checklist and evidence examples.
steps: Review the previous handoff. Create the integration branch and port the chosen UI and module wiring without deleting the useful source versions.
Fix dependencies, including Gradio, and add one configuration loader and environment example. Keep credentials out of files and logs.
Run the existing lightweight tests and launch the UI in an explicit not-ready state. Document installation, data location and launch commands.
days.done: The application starts from documented commands, reports missing data clearly and has a saved setup and test log.
days.learn: A launchable application needs its dependencies, configuration and entry point to agree.

days.title: Connect a real model and remove false success
days.why: A fixed mock answer must never appear as financial analysis when the actual provider fails.
days.need: The configured application and status contract from Days 1 and 2.
steps: Verify one real provider and model on the demo machine. Put the confirmed model identifier in configuration and construct an explicit API client.
Remove automatic mock fallback and process-wide credential mutation. Keep mock mode available only through an explicit test setting.
Return service_error for provider failures and insufficient_evidence when context is absent. Save one real-call check and one deliberate failure check.
days.done: A real model call works; invalid credentials and empty evidence cannot return the fixed mock financial answer.
days.learn: Model access failure and missing source evidence are different outcomes and must remain visible.

days.title: Parse one supported annual report
days.why: One fully checked filing is a feasible foundation for the reduced schedule. Downloaded files alone are not searchable evidence.
days.need: The filing choice, evidence schema and data path already recorded.
steps: Record the exact accession, company, report fiscal year, original URL, local path and checksum for one Apple 10-K.
Move the required parsing cells into a repeatable function. Extract bounded sections from Items 1A, 7 and 8 and relevant statement tables.
Emit narrative and table records separately, preserving source locations, table titles, comparative periods and declared units. Save a parsing summary.
days.done: One command parses the declared filing into traceable narrative and table records; the table of contents is not treated as risk-factor evidence.
days.learn: The filing year and the comparative year of a table value are separate pieces of metadata.

days.title: Build and reopen the persistent index
days.why: Search must use the intended parsed report and return the same records after restart or repeated ingestion.
days.need: The Day 4 parsed records and original source manifest.
steps: Index the supported records with the existing MiniLM embedder and Chroma. Use deterministic IDs containing filing identity, evidence type and location.
Preserve source metadata, parent-table links and embedding identity. Replace that filing cleanly so shortened reruns do not leave stale records.
Re-ingest twice, restart the application and compare IDs and counts. Save one retrieved narrative record and one table record with their sources.
days.done: Repeated ingestion is stable, reopening the index preserves search and every returned record resolves to the supported report.
days.learn: Persistent search is reproducible only when IDs, stored embeddings and source metadata remain consistent.

days.title: Preserve source records through retrieval
days.why: Returning passage text alone loses the information needed to verify the company, period and cited source.
days.need: The Day 5 populated index and evidence contract.
steps: Return complete evidence records through retrieval and the existing reranker. Validate supported filing and value-period filters.
Define dense baseline and table-aware modes with the same generator, calculator and context limit. Baseline chunks retain flattened table facts.
Skip disabled retrieval streams instead of issuing zero-result queries. Handle empty collections and no eligible evidence before generation.
days.done: A retrieved source ID survives ranking; baseline and table-aware modes return structured evidence and fail clearly when no eligible record exists.
days.learn: The baseline measures retrieval changes fairly only when generation and available source facts are matched.

days.title: Finish the source linked question interface
days.why: A user should see the answer and the actual evidence without inspecting the notebook or developer logs.
days.need: The real provider, persistent index and structured retrieval output.
steps: Connect the UI to the selected backend. Show the supported report, question input, retrieval mode and an understandable loading state.
Display answer status, retrieved passages, table title, comparative period, units and original source links. Add the calculation area for later integration.
Check a narrative question, table question, empty input and missing-evidence case. Verify invalid credentials give a service error and inputs stay session-specific.
days.done: The integrated UI shows real evidence and source links and handles the four checked cases without notebook execution.
days.learn: Showing an answer is not enough; the interface must let the reader verify the source and recognize a failure.

days.title: Repair the tables needed for the demonstration
days.why: Financial values are useful only when their row labels, comparative periods and scale survive parsing.
days.need: The Day 7 evidence display and original annual report.
steps: Select three representative financial tables from the supported report. Check their headers, units, parentheses, blank values and comparative-year columns.
Create self-describing row records with parent-table links. Keep raw values and normalized numeric values and exclude duplicate narrative table copies.
Save small hand-checked fixtures and refresh the index using the existing command. Verify the displayed source locations against the original report.
days.done: The three selected tables have source-checked values, labels, years and units; row records expand back to their original table.
days.learn: Table-aware retrieval preserves relationships that disappear when a grid is flattened into unrelated text.

days.title: Add a small source checked calculator
days.why: The model can explain a calculation, but arithmetic should run in predictable code using values actually retrieved.
days.need: The normalized values and parent references from Day 8.
steps: Connect the existing math helpers to the answer path for sum, difference and percentage change. Use typed operations and evidence-linked operands.
Normalize the supported currency scale, preserve the requested periods and reject absent or incompatible operands. Do not execute arbitrary generated code.
Show the formula, substituted values, result and unit. Check positive-year growth, a negative amount, missing evidence and a zero denominator.
days.done: A demonstrated calculation uses cited operands and checked arithmetic; zero-base or insufficient-data cases explain why no growth result is available.
days.learn: A calculated answer needs correct inputs, units and periods as well as correct arithmetic.

days.title: Keep complete evidence in the model context
days.why: A relevant table may be retrieved but still lose its important rows when a character slice cuts the model input.
days.need: The row records, source-linked calculator and two retrieval modes.
steps: Replace the 4000-character table slice with complete record selection under the configured input budget. Retain headers, units and required operand rows.
Preserve the included evidence IDs in the answer contract. Reject references or calculations that cannot be matched to included records.
Check a long-table fixture and an unsupported-period question. Keep baseline and enhanced generation settings and total context budget the same.
days.done: The required rows reach final context, every citation maps to included evidence and unsupported periods produce clear abstention.
days.learn: Retrieval quality is lost if context assembly removes the information needed to answer the question.

days.title: Prepare the small evaluation and report outline
days.why: The submission needs a modest, honest test rather than a broad accuracy claim that the schedule cannot substantiate.
days.need: The working integrated app, original report and matched retrieval modes.
steps: Create 14 questions with source locations and checked answers: six narrative, four table, two calculation and two unanswerable cases.
Reserve seven development and seven held-out IDs before tuning: each split has three narrative, two table, one calculation and one unanswerable case.
Freeze a scoring checklist for answers, units, source support, evidence recall and timing. Create the report outline and an evaluation-results template.
days.done: A versioned 14-case question file, fixed seven plus seven split, scoring rubric and report outline exist. No test answers are used to tune retrieval.
days.learn: A small source-checked test supports a precise claim about this report; it does not establish broad financial accuracy.

days.title: Independently verify labels and freeze the split
days.why: The answers used to score the app need an independent source check so a mistaken gold label does not reward a wrong result.
days.need: The Day 11 question file, split and original source records.
steps: Independently verify all 14 answers and supporting locations against the original report. Correct labels without moving difficult test questions into development.
Map baseline and table-aware records to the same source locations. Confirm repeatable record counts and the intended embedding version.
Run only the seven development questions to check the scoring process. Correct a blocking index or metadata defect and record the resulting version.
days.done: Every gold case has an independent verification record and the split is locked. Only development examples have been used to guide corrections.
days.learn: Citation identity and scoring must stay fair when baseline and enhanced chunk boundaries differ.

days.title: Verify final answers and freeze evaluation settings
days.why: The final model, calculation path and failure states must be fixed before the reserved questions are run.
days.need: The checked labels, development results and real generation provider.
steps: Recheck model-unavailable, no-evidence, incompatible-unit and zero-denominator paths using development cases or dedicated fixtures.
Confirm mock mode is rejected by the real evaluation path. Keep the same model, prompt, calculator and context budget for both retrieval modes.
Freeze the code revision and run settings. Save a generation and calculation handoff explaining how to run the reserved cases and record failures.
days.done: A frozen evaluation revision and configuration exist, with explicit failure checks and no hidden mock fallback.
days.learn: Freezing settings before test evaluation prevents favorable-looking results from being selected through repeated tuning.

days.title: Run the reserved evaluation and capture the demo
days.why: Today measures the frozen app on the seven questions that were kept out of tuning and records what actually works.
days.need: The Day 13 frozen revision, two modes, held-out IDs and scoring rubric.
steps: Run all seven held-out questions in both modes and retain all 14 outputs, included evidence IDs, status, model settings and timing.
Score the six answerable and one unanswerable case per mode. Check sources, numerical periods and units, and compare evidence coverage fairly.
Save the metric table and error notes. Capture a short demo showing a real answer, source, calculation and abstention; label saved results and recordings clearly.
days.done: Fourteen held-out outputs, a scored result table, source audits and a playable backup demo are saved, including failures.
days.learn: Measured results may favor either mode. Reporting failures and denominators matters more than promising improvement.

days.title: Write the evidence based final report draft
days.why: The report must explain the delivered system and actual measurements, with a clear boundary around the reduced scope.
days.need: The report outline, source manifest and Day 14 results.
steps: Draft the problem, one-report corpus, parsing method, table representation and implemented architecture using the saved handoff notes.
Insert the actual results with counts and explain source examples, limitations and unsupported layouts. Mark chart analysis and broad benchmarks as future work.
Include the seven-member contribution log, source references and AI-assistance disclosure draft. Add setup and calculator sections from the existing handoffs.
days.done: A complete short report draft explains methods, actual results, limitations and all seven contributions; no unimplemented feature is claimed.
days.learn: The report should describe the submitted software and evidence, including its limitations, rather than repeat an earlier ambitious proposal.

days.title: Audit results and review the report
days.why: A separate review checks that the saved outputs justify the reported conclusions and that retrieval behavior is explained correctly.
days.need: The Day 15 report draft and all evaluation artifacts.
steps: Independently review the 14 saved outputs and recompute the reported counts. Check that incorrect periods, units and unsupported answers are scored as failures.
Classify remaining errors as parsing, retrieval, context, calculation or provider failures. Correct the report and add an annotated question-to-source walkthrough.
Fix only a reproducible release blocker. If a fix affects outputs, version it, rerun both modes and label the results as reused-test regression results.
days.done: The report and result table have an independent review record. Every change has an explained effect on the saved evidence.
days.learn: After the test run, investigate and report errors instead of treating the test answers as another tuning set.

days.title: Package data and prepare the final presentation
days.why: The evaluator needs a clear source inventory and a short explanation of how the project works, alongside the runnable code.
days.need: The reviewed report, final source revision and ingestion instructions.
steps: Package the filing manifest, small fixtures, record-count summary and deterministic index rebuild instructions. Verify every original source link.
Assemble a short presentation from the report: problem, workflow, table treatment, calculated answer, actual comparison and limitations.
Create the release checklist and archive inventory. Check that the report, results, presentation, demo and contribution log refer to the intended versions.
days.done: The data package, short presentation and release inventory are ready for a clean-machine check.
days.learn: Data identity and source instructions are part of reproducibility, even when large raw files are not committed to Git.

days.title: Run the final clean machine and release check
days.why: The last full technical check protects delivery from hidden local dependencies and missing files.
days.need: The Day 17 release inventory, runnable source and both saved retrieval modes.
steps: Build or restore the index on a fresh environment using the included instructions. Run a known question and confirm its cited source and calculation.
Check credentials, runtime requirements and the app launch command. Keep the verified native launch path; add no cloud deployment or new container dependency.
Recheck critical failure paths, open the report, slides and demo, then freeze and back up the archive. Save its checksum, exact revision and launch evidence.
days.done: The final archive launches from documented inputs, all delivery files open and a backup plus verification log are ready.
days.learn: The release check proves the project can leave the original developer machine without losing its data or setup knowledge.

days.title: Complete final verification and deliver the project
days.why: November 17 is the final project delivery deadline. Use the verified package and retain proof of what was delivered.
days.need: The Day 18 frozen archive, report, presentation, demo and verification log.
steps: Check the exact package against the official delivery checklist. Verify seven correct names, final links, report results and contribution records.
Perform a short final demo using the frozen build or transparently labeled backup video. Make only necessary document corrections.
Deliver or submit before the confirmed November 17 cutoff and retain the receipt and exact archive. If the official portal opens later, retain this frozen ready-to-submit release.
days.done: The project is complete by November 17, with its final package and verification record delivered. If submission is open, the receipt is retained; otherwise the frozen release is ready.
days.learn: Finishing by the internal deadline means the code, evidence and documents are complete together, without relying on later development.
